entries.title: Warning before a mayor leaves
entries.text: In the last 24 hours of a term, a portfolio flip is marked when the mayor's or minister's perk kept its price down, for example Paul leaves in 5h – price may rise back.

entries.title: The next minister counts too
entries.text: The election warning now also looks at the perk the runner-up would bring along as minister.

entries.title: More dungeon chest items for Paul
entries.text: Marauder now also lists Wither Blood, the three Necron scrolls, Giant Tooth, Sadan's Brooch, Dark Orb, Necromancer's Brooch, Spirit Bone and Spirit Wing.

entries.title: Election warning in the portfolio
entries.text: While an election runs, a flip is marked when the leading candidate has a perk that brings more of that item, for example Diana and Griffin Feathers.

entries.title: More Diana items
entries.text: The radar now also lists Braided Griffin Feather, Chimera I, Fateful Stinger, Brain Food and the shards of the mythological creatures for Diana's Mythological Ritual.

entries.title: Max. flips explained
entries.text: The help text for Max. flips now says what the portfolio does: it picks the flips that earn the most with your budget, up to that many.

entries.title: Max. flips, up to 21
entries.text: Parallel flips is now Max. flips and stops at 21, because the bazaar allows 21 open orders. A higher value you had set became 21.

entries.title: Better choice of flips
entries.text: The portfolio now picks the flips that earn the most together, so a small budget is no longer spent on a few big items when more flips would earn more.

entries.title: Flips in use
entries.text: The portfolio shows how many of your flips it uses, and at 21 flips it says how much the market can take right now.

entries.title: Expensive items in the portfolio
entries.text: The portfolio now asks for a minimum turnover in coins per week instead of a number of items, so pricey items that sell steadily can get a stake.

entries.title: Portfolio min. margin
entries.text: The portfolio has its own margin floor, 3% to start with, so items that trade a lot can take part even if your Opportunities list asks for more.

entries.title: How many flips would use your capital
entries.text: When your parallel flips hold capital back, the note says how many flips would use how much, with the estimated profit per hour.

entries.title: No cap per flip in Simple mode
entries.text: Simple mode no longer limits one flip to an even share of your capital; a flip gets as much as the item trades.

entries.title: Portfolio fills the best flips first
entries.text: Your capital is no longer split evenly: the flips with the best return get as much as the item trades, up to your Max. capital per flip. Parallel flips is only the most flips you run.

entries.title: Clearer note in Simple mode
entries.text: When capital stays unused in Simple mode, the note says why and sends you to Pro mode, where the setting can be changed.

entries.title: Portfolio uses your whole capital
entries.text: Coins one flip cannot use now go to the other flips, up to your Max. capital per flip and never more than an item trades.

entries.title: Why capital stays unused
entries.text: If part of your capital is left over, the portfolio says what limits it and which setting to raise.

entries.title: Return per hour
entries.text: The portfolio shows the capital in use, the profit per hour and the return per hour in percent.

entries.title: Settings open as a sheet
entries.text: The settings now slide up from the bottom instead of pushing the list down. Changes count once you tap Apply; Reset fills in the defaults.

entries.title: Filter button
entries.text: In Pro mode the Filter button next to the search opens only the filters of the tab you are on, and its number says how many you changed.

entries.title: Filter chips
entries.text: Every filter you changed shows as a small chip above the list. Tap its X to put it back to the default.

entries.title: Simple and Pro mode
entries.text: Simple shows only flips, opportunities and the numbers you need for them; Pro shows everything, as before. You stay in Pro and can switch at the top of the settings.

entries.title: Hints where you need them
entries.text: The first time a feature shows up, a short note explains it, for example what suspicious means or how NPC and craft flips work. Tap Got it and it stays away; the ? at the top brings all hints back.

entries.title: Shorter tour, clearer help
entries.text: The tour now starts with what a flip is and leads straight into the setup. How it works is a list you unfold, with new entries for suspicious, favorites, NPC and craft flips.

entries.title: Portfolio respects your max. capital
entries.text: The portfolio never puts more into one flip than your Max. capital per flip. Settings that had the same name now say what they belong to.

entries.title: Event timing
entries.text: The event radar now learns what prices did around past events: once an item moved the same way three times, it says how much it usually changes and when to buy and sell. Based on past events, not a guarantee.

entries.title: Mayor terms
entries.text: Below the mayor you see which items are expected to be cheaper while their perks are active and why, and after three terms what really happened.

entries.title: Event alerts in the app
entries.text: The Android app can notify you about three hours before an event with a confirmed pattern and when a new mayor takes office. Both switches are in the settings and off by default.

entries.title: More realistic forge profit
entries.text: Profit/forge hour no longer assumes you can sell everything a quick recipe makes. It is now capped by your market share of what is bought per hour, and each card says what limits it.

entries.title: Derpy's tax
entries.text: While Derpy is mayor, forge results sold on the Auction House are calculated with the higher tax, and the card says so.

entries.title: Forge details on item pages
entries.text: The page of a forged item now shows the lowest BIN or sell offer, the ingredients with prices, the forge time and the HotM tier.

entries.title: Forge tab
entries.text: A new tab shows what is worth forging: what the ingredients cost, the profit per item and per forge hour, how long it takes and the HotM tier you need. Results that sell on the Auction House are marked as estimates.

entries.title: Event radar
entries.text: A card above every list shows the mayor, the active perks and the next SkyBlock events with a countdown. Tap a line to see the items that are typically affected.

entries.title: Trend badges
entries.text: An arrow on each card tells you whether the sell price was rising, falling or flat over the last day, and whether it is below or above its normal price. You can sort by Trend here.

entries.title: Two tours
entries.text: The tour now covers the basics in six steps. A second, optional tour explains portfolio, forge, event radar and trends. Both start from the ? at the top.

entries.title: Pull to refresh you can see
entries.text: Pull down on a list or an item page: an arrow appears below the header, then a spinner while prices load and a short "Updated" when they are in.

entries.title: Nicer touch feedback
entries.text: The light blue flash on every tap is gone. Cards now give way a little and glow orange when you press them, and buttons darken.

entries.title: Search finds every item
entries.text: The search now covers the whole bazaar. Items your filters hide still show up, with a short note why they are not a flip right now.

entries.title: Help screen
entries.text: The new ? at the top opens the tour, the setup, What's new and a short explanation of how the numbers are calculated.

entries.title: App tour
entries.text: A short guided tour explains every part of the app. You can restart it any time in the settings.

entries.title: Setup assistant
entries.text: Three quick questions and the app suggests settings that fit your capital and play style.

entries.title: What's new
entries.text: After an update this window shows you what changed. The full history is in the settings.

entries.title: Help buttons
entries.text: Every setting now has a small ? that explains what it does.

entries.title: Swipe between tabs
entries.text: Swipe left or right on a list to move to the next tab.

entries.title: Portfolio
entries.text: The Opportunities tab now starts with a plan: your capital split over several safe flips, with the total profit per hour.

entries.title: New look
entries.text: Warmer colours, clearer cards and a layout that uses the whole screen on a computer.

entries.title: Item rarity
entries.text: Each card shows the item's rarity as a coloured stripe and a word in the corner.

entries.title: Safer warnings
entries.text: An item is flagged as suspicious when its price is far above what it normally sells for.

entries.title: Provisional items
entries.text: Items with less than 24 hours of price history are marked and kept out of Opportunities.

entries.title: Charts with values
entries.text: Tap or hover a chart on the detail page to read the exact values.

entries.title: Opportunities
entries.text: A tab that shows only flips that are stable, liquid and within your budget.

entries.title: Market alerts
entries.text: The Android app can notify you when a new opportunity shows up.

entries.title: Price history
entries.text: Every item has a detail page with price and margin charts.

entries.title: Stability score
entries.text: A score from 0 to 100 tells you how reliable a flip has been.

entries.title: NPC and craft flips
entries.text: Two more tabs for selling to NPCs and for crafting.

entries.title: Item pictures
entries.text: Items are shown with their icons.

entries.title: First version
entries.text: Live bazaar flips ranked by profit after tax, with filters and favorites.
